watches.name: Vendetta II Automatic Wandering Hour Oxblood Black
watches.description: The Vendetta II Automatic Wandering Hour is more sleek, legible, and robust than the original. It utilizes our custom wandering hour movement, putting the typically unattainable wandering hour timepiece within the grasp of most watch enthusiasts. The Vendetta II is surprisingly easy to read. The time is read at the bottom of the watch below the beveled crystal, where the hour glides along from right to left, pointing to the minutes. The cycle repeats as the next hour comes into view at the beginning of the minute track, while up above the Geneva gear mechanism shifts the hours to their next place in the sequence. We developed the world’s first modular minute track system for the Vendetta. Alternate minute dials can be brought into the time-telling area by rotating the secondary crown. These additional displays have different minute layouts and colors, so you can customize your watch’s minute track at any time, essentially giving you three different styles in one watch. We doubled the original Vendetta’s water resistance by using screw-down crowns and paired it with a durable two-tone rubber strap for a watch you can take virtually anywhere.

watches.name: Xeriscope Automatic Black Tan Original Collector's Edition
watches.description: ORIGINAL COLLECTOR'S LIMITED EDITION - BRAND NEW NEVER TO BE MADE AGAIN LAST ONE! There's nothing quite like a mechanical watch. The many parts of a machine all working in unison completely viewable from the front is a rare sight these days. The Xeriscope Automatic by Xeric is a bold, modern & industrial example of these favorite features. A fully-exposed, mechanical movement is the hour display - a beating mechanical heart, the mainspring of the watch, pumps life into this complex time machine. Its innovative time display with a unique double-sided minute halo hand features a power reserve meter to show how much power has been stored in the watch - no batteries needed. The Xeriscope deconstructs typical watch functionality with easy-to-read originality. Need to know what time it is at home when traveling or if it's too late to call where your better half is? No problem, the second time zone of the Xeriscope Automatic can be set to any other location on the planet. Its case is layered in panels of surgical grade stainless steel bolted together into one solid time machine for the wrist, and the rotor (oscillating mass) that generates the power supply to the movement can be seen from the porthole caseback viewing crystal. The end result is a design perfected with focus on style and legibility.

watches.name: Timeline Retrograde Automatic Black
watches.description: The Timeline Retrograde is powered by the high end Miyota 9015 movement with a custom built retrograde complication. Every 60 minutes the flyback mechanism launches the minute hand back to zero, in the most dramatic and satisfying way, unlike any other traditional watch. And every 12-hour transition from AM to PM or vice versa, the hour hand does the same. The retrograde complication enables the dial to have a linear time display, with intuitive, easy to read time telling, but completely unique in design. The Timeline Retrograde features excellent dial finishing with applied indices and a sunken date window. The 38mm stainless steel case is sized to be comfortable on the wrist. Brushed and polished finishing on the case and bracelet make it pop, and an exhibition caseback shows the rotor. Production is limited to just 999 pieces per color.

watches.description: Exclusive edition of the Xeric Planetarium GMT. Limited to 314 pieces. Inspired by antique orreries and the mesmerizing mechanics that mimic planetary motion, this timepiece transforms timekeeping into a celestial experience. Dimensional hour, minute, and second indications are expressed through orbiting spheres, while the GMT hour is indicated by a transiting rocketship. watches.name: NASA Trappist-1 Sapphire Blue Moon
watches.description: All Trappist-1 NASA Edition has back-filled luminous hands and silkscreened dials for stargazing. The Orbiting Planetary System consists of glowing Super-LumiNova™ indices and planets to help space explorers keep track of time as they travel in the darkest regions of the universe. The inner luminous planet represents the hours while the outer luminous planet shows the minutes, all while orbiting around the central axis. The constellation-like seconds hand sweeps across the dial similar to comets streaking across the night sky and once every minute it aligns to complete the Trappist-1 star map dial. The Trappist-1 is built around a high-torque, Seiko VH31 movement with semi-sweeping seconds hand. The caseback features engraved 50th anniversary commemorative artwork of the Apollo 11 mission patch. The grille of the Trappist-1 resembles the Cupola and gives you a sense of looking out into space. Each of the twelve support bridges also doubles as an hour marker. The domed crystal is made from ultra-scratch resistant s apphire glass. The straps are made from U.S. Horween leather which is ribbed and stitched to pay tribute to the articulated ridge-lines seen on space gloves. In honor of the year of the moon landing, only 1969 pieces of each Trappist-1 NASA Edition colorway will be made and each watch will be individually numbered.

watches.name: Invertor+ Automatic Navy White Lume Limited Edition
watches.description: The Invertor+ Automatic features an updated rotor design and is part of an ultra-limited edition of only 50 pieces per color. The Invertor was a groundbreaking inverted movement design - the only watch of its kind from an independent brand that retails for under $3,000. The winding automatic rotor is displayed on the front of the watch instead of the underside, giving the wearer a true appreciation for the mechanical beauty of this machine. In order to create the Invertor, we developed a new proprietary module for the Miyota 9000 calibre automatic movement. The module mechanically makes the watch run backwards, but when the movement is flipped upside down in the case, time then reads correctly. The unique curved case and crystal shape as well as the impressive mechanics allow you to see the time and automatic rotor in the same glance.

watches.name: NASA Apollo 15 Moonphase Blue Moon
watches.description: In 1971, the Apollo 15 mission took lunar exploration to the next level when they introduced the first lunar roving vehicle, allowing astronauts to venture out and collect samples further than ever before. 50 years later, the Xeric NASA Apollo 15 Collection celebrates American ingenuity with a movement that tracks the current phase of the moon through its 29.5 day cycle. Using our signature method of time telling with orbiting moons as watch hands, the hours and minutes float above the miniature solar system backdrop. The grille was inspired by a spacecraft window giving the sense of looking out at the stars. Swiss Super-LumiNova is printed on the inner and outer edge for improved legibility in both light (and especially) dark conditions. To top it all off, there are nods to the Apollo 15 mission throughout the design. Like an astronaut’s helmet, the curved sapphire crystal provides the ultimate in scratch resistance while an anti-reflective coating reduces glare. Fashioned after astronaut gloves, the Apollo 15 straps feature articulated ridges and are crafted from premium American-made Horween leather. The Apollo 15 features a coin-engraved solid steel caseback depicting the lunar rover where it sits today and commemorating the 50th anniversary of its arrival on the surface of the moon.

watches.name: Halograph II Automatic Limited Edition Silver
watches.description: The Halograph II Automatic features Xeric's innovative signature display and halo hands which float over the arcs to encircle the time. The inner arcs display the hours and the outer arcs display the minutes. The time can easily be read through the two halo hands. As the halo reaches the end of its track, a new halo appears on the opposite side, similar to a retrograde display. Two secondary displays were integrated into the movement grille. The day/night window on the left displays your current position relative to the sun. The window on the right is a running second display. These features are printed on transparent discs for an unobstructed view of the large open balance wheel. The Miyota 82S7's exposed balance wheel gives a glimpse into the mechanical engine that keeps track of time. The automatic rotor on the back winds the watch using the kinetic energy of your motion, which means the watch will stay perpetually wound when you wear it - no batteries are required. The straps are made using premium, full-grain leather from Horween, one of the oldest continuously running tanneries in the United States.¬† The straps also feature a quick change springbar system allowing you to swap out different straps for every occasion. To make each Halograph II Automatic as unique as you are, Xeric will be limiting each colorway to only 999 pieces. Each watch will be individually numbered.

This limited-edition timepiece transforms mathematical precision into bold design, featuring radial time display, Roman numerals, digital-style indicators, and laser-cut sapphire glass hands that glide above the dial with striking clarity. Powered by the high-beat Miyota 9039 automatic movement, the Omnigraph delivers exceptional accuracy and reliability. Crafted for everyday wear, the Omnigraph features a 40mm stainless steel case, domed sapphire crystal, and a comfortable Italian Saffiano leather strap. Available in multiple colorways that blend vintage cues with contemporary styling, it’s a refined piece of functional art for collectors and design enthusiasts alike. The Omnigraph will be offered in limited quantities—only 500 pieces per colorway.

watches.name: NASA Apollo 15 Moonphase Blue Supernova
watches.description: In 1971, the Apollo 15 mission took lunar exploration to the next level when they introduced the first lunar roving vehicle, allowing astronauts to venture out and collect samples further than ever before. 50 years later, the Xeric NASA Apollo 15 Collection celebrates American ingenuity with a movement that tracks the current phase of the moon through its 29.5 day cycle. Using our signature method of time telling with orbiting moons as watch hands, the hours and minutes float above the miniature solar system backdrop. The grille was inspired by a spacecraft window giving the sense of looking out at the stars. Swiss Super-LumiNova is printed on the inner and outer edge for improved legibility in both light (and especially) dark conditions. To top it all off, there are nods to the Apollo 15 mission throughout the design. Like an astronaut’s helmet, the curved sapphire crystal provides the ultimate in scratch resistance while an anti-reflective coating reduces glare. Fashioned after astronaut gloves, the Apollo 15 straps feature articulated ridges and are crafted from premium American-made Horween leather. The Apollo 15 features a coin-engraved solid steel caseback depicting the lunar rover where it sits today and commemorating the 50th anniversary of its arrival on the surface of the moon.

watches.name: Soloscope II Automatic Blue Tan
watches.description: The Soloscope II Automatic has been completely redesigned and upgraded from the original. Powered by the venerable Miyota 8217 automatic movement with date function, a 40 hour power reserve and a custom-designed rotor that can be seen through the case back. A skeletonized hour hand comes into view as it rotates over a luminous background while the halo hand encircles the minutes. The left-hand side of the watch is an AM/PM indicator and can alternatively be used to read the hours. The new case design features a slimmer profile with a colorful anodized aluminum ring, integrated lugs, and anti-reflective sapphire glass. When the lights go out, the Soloscope II really shines. We redesigned our signature halo hands so they glow brighter and longer, and the dial features an abundance of Super-LumiNova; nicknamed "the jellyfish" because of the impressive glowing pattern it makes when the watch is turned on its side in the dark. As always, our straps are made from American-sourced Horween leather and quick release mechanism for tool-less strap changes. The Soloscope II is limited to just 999 pieces per color.

watches.name: Vendetta II Automatic Wandering Hour Black Cyan Lume
watches.description: The Vendetta II Automatic Wandering Hour is more sleek, legible, and robust than the original. It utilizes our custom wandering hour movement, putting the typically unattainable wandering hour timepiece within the grasp of most watch enthusiasts. The Vendetta II is surprisingly easy to read. The time is read at the bottom of the watch below the beveled crystal, where the hour glides along from right to left, pointing to the minutes. The cycle repeats as the next hour comes into view at the beginning of the minute track, while up above the Geneva gear mechanism shifts the hours to their next place in the sequence. We developed the world’s first modular minute track system for the Vendetta. Alternate minute dials can be brought into the time-telling area by rotating the secondary crown. These additional displays have different minute layouts and colors, so you can customize your watch’s minute track at any time, essentially giving you three different styles in one watch. We doubled the original Vendetta’s water resistance by using screw-down crowns and paired it with a durable two-tone rubber strap for a watch you can take virtually anywhere.

The Orbiting Planetary System consists of glowing Super-LumiNova indices and planets to help space explorers keep track of time as they travel in the darkest regions of the universe. The inner luminous planet represents the hours while the outer luminous planet shows the minutes, all while orbiting around the central axis. The Trappist-1 Automatic has a Miyota 8215 self-winding movement that generates power as you wear it. The mechanical movement is made in Japan and is known for its precision and reliability. Each automatic movement comes equipped with a proprietary solar system rotor that can be appreciated through the exhibition crystal on the caseback. The Trappist-1 Automatic has a power reserve of 42 hours. The grille of the Trappist-1 resembles the Cupola and gives you a sense of looking out into space. Each of the twelve support bridges also doubles as an hour marker. The domed crystal is made from ultra-scratch resistant s apphire glass. The straps are made from U.S. Horween leather which is ribbed and stitched to pay tribute to the articulated ridge-lines seen on space gloves. watches.name: Regulator Automatic Cotton Candy
watches.description: The Regulator Automatic breaks down timekeeping into its purest form, separating the hours, minutes, and seconds into distinctly isolated functions. To pull this off, we turned to the mechanical regulator clocks of the 18th century, which were used when legibility was essential, and sometimes meant life or death. Railway conductors, mariners--and even Captain Cook on his voyages around the globe--relied on regulator clocks’ clear and simple way of time telling. Separating functions into isolated subdials allows the reader to see each hand clearly and distinctly. In an impressive mechanical feat, the movement powers hours, minutes, and seconds on separate posts rather than one central pinion. The Regulator Automatic uses a high quality self-winding Miyota movement that we’ve customized with a uniquely designed and precisely balanced rotor. We’re of the mindset that functional minimalism doesn’t equate to stark, boring design. The Regulator features raised and sunken elements to accentuate the simple timekeeping of each hand, while also giving you a glimpse into the automatic movement that powers the timepiece. A subtle AM/PM indicator ring is built into the 24-hour display, and a split display for the seconds adds a little Xeric DNA to the watch. We’re proud to bring you our handcrafted watches made from the best materials. A sapphire crystal, premium leather, and an unparalleled design make the watch an incredible deal. These stunning time machines are individually numbered and limited to just 999 pieces per color.

watches.description: The limited-edition Xeric Halograph III Chrono channels the boundary-pushing spirit of the 1960s, blending vintage watchmaking with bold automotive design. watches.name: Timeline Retrograde Automatic Purple
watches.description: The Timeline Retrograde is powered by the high end Miyota 9015 movement with a custom built retrograde complication. Every 60 minutes the flyback mechanism launches the minute hand back to zero, in the most dramatic and satisfying way, unlike any other traditional watch. And every 12-hour transition from AM to PM or vice versa, the hour hand does the same. The retrograde complication enables the dial to have a linear time display, with intuitive, easy to read time telling, but completely unique in design. The Timeline Retrograde features excellent dial finishing with applied indices and a sunken date window. The 38mm stainless steel case is sized to be comfortable on the wrist. Brushed and polished finishing on the case and bracelet make it pop, and an exhibition caseback shows the rotor. Production is limited to just 999 pieces per color.

watches.name: Halograph II Chrono Rose Gold Indigo
watches.description: The Halograph II Chrono tells time using our signature split display, which we argue is easier to tell the time than a traditional clock. Simply read the time inside each circle at the top of the watch. The inner circle shows the hour, and the outer circle shows the minutes. And when the lights go out, the Swiss SuperLumiNova transforms the time-telling into that of a clock with a traditional hour and minute hand. We took our favorite parts of the Halograph and upgraded them with an automotive twist. Bold colors and a sleek new case design take the Halograph in a direction it has never gone before. The Halograph II Chrono runs on a precise Miyota chronograph movement with linear subdials displayed at the bottom of the dial, like the gauges on the dash of a modern race car. The case is lugless, like the Automatic, with an anodized aluminum accent ring and a solid smooth leather strap with full stitching. Hand crafted from the best materials--a stainless steel case with precisely brushed and polished finishes, a scratch-resistant sapphire crystal with an anti-reflective coating, and American Horween or Italian leather racing straps.

watches.name: Invertor II Automatic Gunmetal Orange

The watch is powered by a skeletonized Japanese automatic movement on full display through the crystal. The space pod-like case features a side viewing window that tells the time in a unique linear format. This novel display utilizes a revolving drum to show the time in increasing 15-minute increments with 5-minute marks printed on the top. The strap is made from the best American-made Horween leather with a built-in quick-release system for easy strap changes.

watches.name: NASA Artemis Tumbler Automatic Orion
watches.description: The tumbling satellite complication of the NASA Artemis Tumbler Automatic tells the time in a mesmerizing way, utilizing our proprietary tumbling hour automatic movement. To read the time, simply look at the time-telling section at the bottom of the dial where the minute track lines are located. Follow the current hour as it overlaps the 0 to 60 minute track lines and points to the current minute. Every hour a new hand will glide along the minute track. Easily change the look of the minute track by rotating the bezel, allowing you to choose whether to read the time in 5, 10, or 15 minute increments; lock your choice into place with the screw down crown. The Super-LumiNova dial, hands, and bezel all glow in a variety of ways. A scratch-resistant domed sapphire crystal covers the dial, and the stainless steel case gives you a glimpse of the mechanics through the back of the watch. Being completely mechanical, it doesn’t require batteries. The custom luminous rotor depicts the lunar surface surrounded by stars and the pale blue dot of the Earth in the distance. The watch will come with both a brushed stainless steel bracelet and a 2-tone silicone strap, which are easily interchangeable using our quick release system.

watches.name: NASA Trappist-1 Sapphire Black Hole
watches.description: All Trappist-1 NASA Edition has back-filled luminous hands and silkscreened dials for stargazing. The Orbiting Planetary System consists of glowing Super-LumiNova™ indices and planets to help space explorers keep track of time as they travel in the darkest regions of the universe. The inner luminous planet represents the hours while the outer luminous planet shows the minutes, all while orbiting around the central axis. The constellation-like seconds hand sweeps across the dial similar to comets streaking across the night sky and once every minute it aligns to complete the Trappist-1 star map dial. watches.name: NASA Apollo 15 Automatic Lunar Lander
watches.description: In 1971, the Apollo 15 mission took lunar exploration to the next level when they introduced the first lunar roving vehicle, allowing astronauts to venture out and collect samples further than ever before. 50 years later, the Xeric NASA Apollo 15 Collection celebrates American ingenuity u sing our signature method of time telling with orbiting moons as watch hands, the hours and minutes float above the miniature solar system backdrop. The grille was inspired by a spacecraft window giving the sense of looking out at the stars. Swiss Super-LumiNova is printed on the inner and outer edge for improved legibility in both light (and especially) dark conditions. To top it all off, there are nods to the Apollo 15 mission throughout the design. Like an astronaut’s helmet, the curved sapphire crystal provides the ultimate in scratch resistance while an anti-reflective coating reduces glare. Fashioned after astronaut gloves, the Apollo 15 straps feature articulated ridges and are crafted from premium American-made Horween leather. The Apollo 15 features a coin-engraved solid steel caseback depicting the lunar rover where it sits today and commemorating the 50th anniversary of its arrival on the surface of the moon.

watches.name: Vendetta II Automatic Wandering Hour Black Gray Red
watches.description: The Vendetta II Automatic Wandering Hour is more sleek, legible, and robust than the original. It utilizes our custom wandering hour movement, putting the typically unattainable wandering hour timepiece within the grasp of most watch enthusiasts. The Vendetta II is surprisingly easy to read. The time is read at the bottom of the watch below the beveled crystal, where the hour glides along from right to left, pointing to the minutes. The cycle repeats as the next hour comes into view at the beginning of the minute track, while up above the Geneva gear mechanism shifts the hours to their next place in the sequence. We developed the world’s first modular minute track system for the Vendetta. Alternate minute dials can be brought into the time-telling area by rotating the secondary crown. These additional displays have different minute layouts and colors, so you can customize your watch’s minute track at any time, essentially giving you three different styles in one watch. We doubled the original Vendetta’s water resistance by using screw-down crowns and paired it with a durable two-tone rubber strap for a watch you can take virtually anywhere.

It utilizes our custom wandering hour movement, putting the typically unattainable wandering hour timepiece within the grasp of most watch enthusiasts. The Vendetta II is surprisingly easy to read. The time is read at the bottom of the watch below the beveled crystal, where the hour glides along from right to left, pointing to the minutes. The cycle repeats as the next hour comes into view at the beginning of the minute track, while up above the Geneva gear mechanism shifts the hours to their next place in the sequence. We developed the world’s first modular minute track system for the Vendetta. Alternate minute dials can be brought into the time-telling area by rotating the secondary crown. These additional displays have different minute layouts and colors, so you can customize your watch’s minute track at any time, essentially giving you three different styles in one watch. We doubled the original Vendetta’s water resistance by using screw-down crowns and paired it with a durable two-tone rubber strap for a watch you can take virtually anywhere.

watches.name: Scrambler Automatic Wandering Hour Rose Gold Ocean
watches.description: The Scrambler Automatic takes design cues from vintage 1970s watch cases, while taking advantage of modern manufacturing and finishing precision today. Powered by our proprietary automatic wandering hour movement, it’s completely mechanical. It never requires batteries and will never die as you wear it. Reading the time looks complicated but is actually quite easy. Simply look at where the hour meets the minutes in the upper viewing window. That’s it. As time passes, the next hour comes into view, and the geneva gear mechanism shifts the hands to their next position. Tiered layering creates a sense of depth that isn’t typically seen in a watch dial, almost giving the appearance that the hands are mechanically excavating down into the dial. We used the best materials to create the Scrambler Automatic – a beautifully brushed case made of 316L stainless steel, colorful anodized aluminum module arms, ribbed American Horween leather straps, and Swiss-made Super-LumiNova minutes and hours. With all of the lume on the Scrambler back-filled in deep wells, this is the brightest Xeric watch to date.

watches.name: NASA Voyager Automatic 1000m Diver Europa
watches.description: Whether it’s deep in the ocean or deep in space, the Voyager Automatic can withstand 100 times the pressure of Earth’s atmosphere. With this 1,000 meter depth rating, we’ve also integrated a helium escape valve into the case, preventing a pressure differential that can occur during deep dives. The watch is powered by the self-winding Seiko NH38 automatic movement. As you wear it, the rotor winds the mainspring, creating stored mechanical energy that powers the watch. The movement is housed in a robust stainless steel case complete with a tactile 120-click rotating bezel fit for divers. The dial features NASA’s iconic “worm” logo and a uniquely layered surface. A thick coating of Super-LumiNova is applied to the hands and dial, extending legibility in the dark. The watch dial is protected by an ultra scratch-resistant sapphire crystal. The caseback features an inlaid replica of “the Golden Record” cover which is found on the outside of the Voyager spacecraft, intended to communicate a story of our world to any intelligent life it could encounter in its journey And we’ve custom molded a new silicone strap which retains a shape reminiscent of ribbed astronaut gloves, and in an array of two-tone colors. Made to withstand extreme conditions, the Voyager Automatic will be your constant companion as you explore your world. Limited Edition: Individually Numbered 1 through 1977

With this 1,000 meter depth rating, we’ve also integrated a helium escape valve into the case, preventing a pressure differential that can occur during deep dives. The watch is powered by the self-winding Seiko NH38 automatic movement. As you wear it, the rotor winds the mainspring, creating stored mechanical energy that powers the watch. The movement is housed in a robust stainless steel case complete with a tactile 120-click rotating bezel fit for divers. The dial features NASA’s iconic “worm” logo and a uniquely layered surface. A thick coating of Super-LumiNova is applied to the hands and dial, extending legibility in the dark. The watch dial is protected by an ultra scratch-resistant sapphire crystal. The caseback features an inlaid replica of “the Golden Record” cover which is found on the outside of the Voyager spacecraft, intended to communicate a story of our world to any intelligent life it could encounter in its journey And we’ve custom molded a new silicone strap which retains a shape reminiscent of ribbed astronaut gloves, and in an array of two-tone colors. Made to withstand extreme conditions, the Voyager Automatic will be your constant companion as you explore your world. Limited Edition: Individually Numbered 1 through 1977

watches.name: NASA Trappist-1 Sapphire Red Dwarf
watches.description: All Trappist-1 NASA Edition has back-filled luminous hands and silkscreened dials for stargazing. The Orbiting Planetary System consists of glowing Super-LumiNova™ indices and planets to help space explorers keep track of time as they travel in the darkest regions of the universe. The inner luminous planet represents the hours while the outer luminous planet shows the minutes, all while orbiting around the central axis. The constellation-like seconds hand sweeps across the dial similar to comets streaking across the night sky and once every minute it aligns to complete the Trappist-1 star map dial. The Trappist-1 is built around a high-torque, Seiko VH31 movement with semi-sweeping seconds hand. The caseback features engraved 50th anniversary commemorative artwork of the Apollo 11 mission patch. The grille of the Trappist-1 resembles the Cupola and gives you a sense of looking out into space. Each of the twelve support bridges also doubles as an hour marker. The domed crystal is made from ultra-scratch resistant s apphire glass. The straps are made from U.S. Horween leather which is ribbed and stitched to pay tribute to the articulated ridge-lines seen on space gloves. In honor of the year of the moon landing, only 1969 pieces of each Trappist-1 NASA Edition colorway will be made and each watch will be individually numbered.

watches.name: Halograph III Automatic Final Lap
watches.description: The sixties were all about pushing the limits--in music, fashion, architecture, space travel, and especially cars. 1966 marked the year the first American car manufacturer won the renowned 24 Hours of Le Mans, making it a major milestone of modern racing in America. At Xeric, we always live by the spirit of the ’60s by pushing boundaries in our watch designs. Inspired by an era of vintage timepieces and striking automotive design, we’re excited to bring you the latest iteration of a classic Xeric watch: the limited edition Halograph III Automatic We took our favorite parts of the Halograph and upgraded them with a retro-automotive twist. Bold colors and a sleek new case design take the Halograph in a direction it has never gone before. Built around the high quality Seiko NH36 automatic movement with a 42-hour power reserve. Without the use of batteries or updates, this mechanical marvel stays running on your wrist as you wear it. The day of the week and date are shown in a unique perforated display at the bottom of the dial. The Halograph III Automatic tells time using our signature split display, which we argue is easier to tell the time than a traditional clock. Simply read the time inside each circle at the top of the watch. The inner circle shows the hour, and the outer circle shows the minutes. And when the lights go out, the Swiss SuperLumiNova transforms the time-telling into that of a clock with a traditional hour and minute hand. Hand crafted from the best materials--a stainless steel case with precisely brushed and polished finishes, a scratch-resistant sapphire crystal with an anti-reflective coating, and American Horween or Italian leather racing straps. The caseback showcases your limited edition number as well as a beautiful coin-engraved depiction of the 1966 Le Mans winner--serving as a reminder to blaze new trails and always move forward.

watches.name: Regulator Automatic Cenote Azul
watches.description: The Regulator Automatic breaks down timekeeping into its purest form, separating the hours, minutes, and seconds into distinctly isolated functions. To pull this off, we turned to the mechanical regulator clocks of the 18th century, which were used when legibility was essential, and sometimes meant life or death. Railway conductors, mariners--and even Captain Cook on his voyages around the globe--relied on regulator clocks’ clear and simple way of time telling. Separating functions into isolated subdials allows the reader to see each hand clearly and distinctly. In an impressive mechanical feat, the movement powers hours, minutes, and seconds on separate posts rather than one central pinion. The Regulator Automatic uses a high quality self-winding Miyota movement that we’ve customized with a uniquely designed and precisely balanced rotor. We’re of the mindset that functional minimalism doesn’t equate to stark, boring design. The Regulator features raised and sunken elements to accentuate the simple timekeeping of each hand, while also giving you a glimpse into the automatic movement that powers the timepiece. A subtle AM/PM indicator ring is built into the 24-hour display, and a split display for the seconds adds a little Xeric DNA to the watch. We’re proud to bring you our handcrafted watches made from the best materials. A sapphire crystal, premium leather, and an unparalleled design make the watch an incredible deal. These stunning time machines are individually numbered and limited to just 999 pieces per color.

watches.name: Halograph Tourbillon Collector's Edition Oxblood
watches.description: The Halograph Tourbillon is the ultimate Xeric watch. The dial features our innovative signature split display and halo hands which float over the arcs to encircle the time. The inner arcs display the hours and the outer arcs display the minutes. The time can easily be read through the two halo hands. As the halo reaches the end of its track, a new halo appears on the opposite side. At the 6 o'clock position you see the balance wheel oscillating back and forth inside the tourbillon cage, which acts as our seconds indicator as it makes one full rotation every 60 seconds. You may be asking, what is a tourbillon? One of the most challenging things watchmakers faced when regulating a mechanical movement was the effects that gravity plays on the caliber or movement. Originally developed by famed watchmaker Abraham-Louis Breguet in 1801. Breguet’s solution was to create an escapement that was constantly in a state of motion. Tourbillons are arguably one the most difficult movements to make by hand. The escapement (hairspring, balance wheel, and pallet fork) is housed in a rotating cage that, because of the constant motion, averages out the effect of gravity when the watch is in different positions. They require a special set of tools and a lot of time to make. The tourbillon mechanism is tiny, weighing in at under a gram, and is usually crafted with more than 40 parts, finished by hand and made from lightweight metals like aluminum and titanium. The straps are made using premium, full-grain leather from Horween, one of the oldest continuously running tanneries in the United States. The clasp design is the same used on high-end luxury watches. Unlike basic deployant clasps, the Halograph Tourbillon clasp allows the end of the long strap to slide between your wrist and the underside of the short strap so no extra leather keepers are required. The strap also has a built-in, quick release springbar system allowing you to swap out different straps for any occasion. Each colorway is limited to only 99 pieces. Each watch is individually numbered.

watches.description: All Trappist-1 NASA Edition has back-filled luminous hands and silkscreened dials for stargazing. The Orbiting Planetary System consists of glowing Super-LumiNova™ indices and planets to help space explorers keep track of time as they travel in the darkest regions of the universe. The inner luminous planet represents the hours while the outer luminous planet shows the minutes, all while orbiting around the central axis. The constellation-like seconds hand sweeps across the dial similar to comets streaking across the night sky and once every minute it aligns to complete the Trappist-1 star map dial. The Trappist-1 is built around a high-torque, Seiko VH31 movement with semi-sweeping seconds hand. The caseback features engraved 50th anniversary commemorative artwork of the Apollo 11 mission patch. The grille of the Trappist-1 resembles the Cupola and gives you a sense of looking out into space. Each of the twelve support bridges also doubles as an hour marker. The domed crystal is made from ultra-scratch resistant s apphire glass. The straps are made from Italian leather which is ribbed and stitched to pay tribute to the articulated ridge-lines seen on space gloves. In honor of the year of the moon landing, only 1969 pieces of each Trappist-1 NASA Edition colorway will be made and each watch will be individually numbered. What is Cerakote? Cerakote is the white ceramic matte finish that comes standard with the Saturn V model. It protects the watch from scratches. Cerakote is not impact resistant and can chip if hit on surfaces.

watches.name: Halograph Tourbillon Collector's Edition Emerald
watches.description: The Halograph Tourbillon is the ultimate Xeric watch. The dial features our innovative signature split display and halo hands which float over the arcs to encircle the time. The inner arcs display the hours and the outer arcs display the minutes. The time can easily be read through the two halo hands. As the halo reaches the end of its track, a new halo appears on the opposite side. At the 6 o'clock position you see the balance wheel oscillating back and forth inside the tourbillon cage, which acts as our seconds indicator as it makes one full rotation every 60 seconds. You may be asking, what is a tourbillon? One of the most challenging things watchmakers faced when regulating a mechanical movement was the effects that gravity plays on the caliber or movement. Originally developed by famed watchmaker Abraham-Louis Breguet in 1801. Breguet’s solution was to create an escapement that was constantly in a state of motion. Tourbillons are arguably one the most difficult movements to make by hand. The escapement (hairspring, balance wheel, and pallet fork) is housed in a rotating cage that, because of the constant motion, averages out the effect of gravity when the watch is in different positions. They require a special set of tools and a lot of time to make. The tourbillon mechanism is tiny, weighing in at under a gram, and is usually crafted with more than 40 parts, finished by hand and made from lightweight metals like aluminum and titanium. The straps are made using premium, full-grain leather from Horween, one of the oldest continuously running tanneries in the United States. The clasp design is the same used on high-end luxury watches. Unlike basic deployant clasps, the Halograph Tourbillon clasp allows the end of the long strap to slide between your wrist and the underside of the short strap so no extra leather keepers are required. The strap also has a built-in, quick release springbar system allowing you to swap out different straps for any occasion. Each colorway is limited to only 99 pieces. Each watch is individually numbered.

watches.name: Regulator Automatic Iron Tiger
watches.description: The Regulator Automatic breaks down timekeeping into its purest form, separating the hours, minutes, and seconds into distinctly isolated functions. To pull this off, we turned to the mechanical regulator clocks of the 18th century, which were used when legibility was essential, and sometimes meant life or death. Railway conductors, mariners--and even Captain Cook on his voyages around the globe--relied on regulator clocks’ clear and simple way of time telling. Separating functions into isolated subdials allows the reader to see each hand clearly and distinctly. In an impressive mechanical feat, the movement powers hours, minutes, and seconds on separate posts rather than one central pinion. The Regulator Automatic uses a high quality self-winding Miyota movement that we’ve customized with a uniquely designed and precisely balanced rotor. We’re of the mindset that functional minimalism doesn’t equate to stark, boring design. The Regulator features raised and sunken elements to accentuate the simple timekeeping of each hand, while also giving you a glimpse into the automatic movement that powers the timepiece. A subtle AM/PM indicator ring is built into the 24-hour display, and a split display for the seconds adds a little Xeric DNA to the watch. We’re proud to bring you our handcrafted watches made from the best materials. A sapphire crystal, premium leather, and an unparalleled design make the watch an incredible deal. These stunning time machines are individually numbered and limited to just 999 pieces per color.

watches.name: Invertor Automatic Gunmetal Brown Limited Edition

The module mechanically makes the watch run backwards, but when the movement is positioned in the case upside down, time reads correctly. Each watch colorway is limited to 999 individually numbered pieces.
